subject: Architecture
title: Buckingham Palace: A House That Became a Symbol
description: A micro-lesson that makes Buckingham Palace: A House That Became a Symbol usable.

hook.text: Buckingham Palace was originally a private townhouse. King George III bought it for his wife.

buildup.text: Queen Victoria was the first monarch to live there. She added the famous east wing balcony.

discovery.text: The palace has 775 rooms, including 78 bathrooms and its own post office and cinema.

twist.text: During World War II, it was bombed nine times. The Queen Mother said she could 'look the East End in the face.'

climax.text: The Changing of the Guard ceremony draws millions of tourists every year to the palace gates.

punchline.text: Started as a townhouse. Now the world's most famous address.

quiz.question: Who was the first monarch to live in Buckingham Palace?

details.summary: Buckingham Palace has 775 rooms including 78 bathrooms and 19 state rooms. Originally built as a townhouse in 1703, it became the official royal residence only in 1837 when Queen Victoria moved in.
details.whyItMatters: Buckingham Palace shows that architectural icons often evolve gradually rather than being designed as masterpieces. Its famous facade is only a century old.
takeaways: 775 rooms including 78 bathrooms in a building from 1703
Became the official royal residence only in 1837 under Victoria
The iconic facade was added as recently as 1913

faq.question: Can the public visit Buckingham Palace?
faq.answer: Parts of the palace open to visitors during summer months when the royal family is at Balmoral. The State Rooms, which host official events, are the main attraction. The Royal Mews and Queen's Gallery are open year-round. Full public access to the palace has never been permitted.

faq.question: Why was the facade redesigned in 1913?
faq.answer: The original soft Caen stone facade had badly deteriorated in London's polluted air. It was refaced in harder Portland stone as part of the Victoria Memorial project. The clean, bright Portland stone created the white appearance now recognized worldwide as the face of British monarchy.
